title: Around the world
goals: Give tourist information about a place using can and can't.
Ask what you can do, where, when, and how, using What, Where, When, How, and Who + can.
Talk about countries, nationalities, and the languages you can speak.
Explain a word you don't know using a kind of, like, and kind of like.
Give examples with like and write lists with commas.
Write a short paragraph for tourists about your city or your food.

learn.title: can / can't: what is possible in a place
learn.html:
You already used can to talk about abilities. Now it also means what is possible or what is allowed in a place: "you can…" or "it's possible to…". It's very common in tourist information.

TypeStructureExample
Affirmativesubject + can + base verbYou can take a ferry to the island.
Negativesubject + can't (cannot) + base verbTourists can't go inside the palace today.
Yes/no questionCan + subject + base verb?Can we take photos here?
Short answerYes, subject + can. / No, subject + can't.Yes, you can. / No, you can't.
  • Can is the same for all subjects: he can, not he cans.
  • After can comes the base verb, without to and without -s.
  • In a guide, you means "anyone": You can see a show every night.

watch.wrong: She can goes to the top of the tower.
watch.right: She can go to the top of the tower.
watch.why: After can, use the base verb, without -s.

watch.wrong: We can to take a bus tour.
watch.right: We can take a bus tour.

watch.wrong: Do tourists can visit the castle?
watch.why: Can forms the question by itself; do/does is not used.

learn.title: Questions with What, Where, When, How, and Who + can
learn.html:
To ask for specific information, we put a question word at the start and can after it: question word + can + subject + base verb.

QuestionPossible answer
What can you do in Cusco?You can visit old temples.
Where can tourists go on a rainy day?They can go to a museum.
When can we visit the castle?You can visit it after ten.
How can I get to the zoo?You can take the bus.
Who can speak Japanese?Aiko can.
What languages can you speak?I can speak Spanish and English.

Order: the subject goes between can and the verb (Where can tourists go?). With who there is no separate subject: Who can help me? If you ask about a noun, put it next to the question word: What languages can you speak?

watch.why: The subject goes between can and the verb.

watch.wrong: What do you can do here?
How I can get to the castle?
watch.right: How can I get to the castle?
watch.why: Can goes before the subject in questions.

learn.title: Explaining words: a kind of, like, and kind of like
learn.html:
When you don't know a word, you can explain it with other words. Three very useful phrases:

PhraseMeaningExample
a kind of + nouna type ofA tamal is a kind of food made with corn.
like + nounsimilar toIt's like a small taco.
kind of like + nouna little bit likeIt's kind of like a sweet bread.
noun + like + examplessuch as, for exampleYou can eat desserts like cake and ice cream.

A kind of takes the article a. With plural: They're a kind of candy (the "type" is singular). Such as also works for giving examples.

watch.right: They are kind of like sugar.
watch.why: The full phrase is kind of like.

watch.right: It is a kind of food.
watch.why: A kind of takes the article a.

watch.wrong: I like desserts like, cake and ice cream.
watch.right: I like desserts like cake and ice cream.

learn.title: Writing lists: the comma
learn.html:
When you name three or more items, separate them with commas and put and before the last one. With only two items there is no comma.

CaseExample
Three or more itemsBangkok is famous for its palaces, temples, and river.
Two itemsI like tea and coffee. (no comma)
Verbs in a listYou can walk, take photos, and eat street food.

The comma before and (the last comma) is optional in English, but it is very common. Don't put a comma if you only join two words with and.

watch.wrong: We saw a bridge a statue and a tower.
watch.right: We saw a bridge, a statue, and a tower.
watch.why: In a list of three, separate the items with commas.
With two items, don't use a comma.

watch.wrong: Mexico, Peru and, Chile are in America.
watch.right: Mexico, Peru, and Chile are in America.
watch.why: The comma goes before and, not after.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• What can you do in…? / You can do a million things. — asking and answering about a place.
  • Can I take a photo here? — Yes, you can. / No, you can't. — asking for permission.
  • Where can I buy…? / How can I get to…? — asking for information.
  • What languages can you speak? — asking about languages.
  • It's a kind of… / It's kind of like… — explaining a word you don't know.
  • Things like… — giving examples: You can buy things like bags and hats.
  • You can't miss it! — it means it's impossible to overlook it.

I think you will love it! It is a little spicy, but it is delicious.

reading.title: A weekend in Oaxaca
reading.intro: Read the travel guide and answer.
paragraphs: Oaxaca is a beautiful city in southern Mexico, and it is a great place for a weekend trip. You can walk around the historic center, visit old churches, and sit at an outdoor café in the main square. It is easy to see a lot in two days.

On Saturday morning, you can take a walking tour of the city. A guide shows you markets, murals, and colorful streets. In the afternoon, you can visit Monte Albán, a very old site on a hill. From the top, you can get a great view of the valleys. You can't go inside every building, but you can take photos of everything.

The food is amazing. Try a tlayuda, which is kind of like a big, crispy tortilla with beans, cheese, and meat. For dessert, you can have hot chocolate. Oaxaca is famous for its mole, chocolate, and cheese.

Where can you buy souvenirs? At the big market, you can find bags, pottery, and clothes. Tourists can also take a bus tour to a small town nearby, but the buses don't go on Sundays. Many people there speak Zapotec and Spanish, and some speak English, too. If you don't speak Spanish, don't worry: you can use a translation app. The weather is warm, so don't forget your hat!

listening.title: At the tourist information desk
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Good morning. Can I help you?
Yes, please. We're in Lisbon for two days. What can we do here?
You can do a lot! You can take a walking tour of the old neighborhood, or you can ride the old yellow tram.
Yes, you can. It's open every day, and from the top you can get a great view of the river.
Wonderful. Where can we buy tickets?
You can buy them here, but you can't buy them at the castle on Sundays.
OK. And where can we eat something typical?
Try a café near the river. The pastries called pastéis de nata are kind of like small egg pies. They're sweet and delicious.
Great. Can we pay with a credit card?
Yes, you can, in most places. But you can't use a card on the tram. Take some cash.
Thank you so much for your help!

items.explain: We're in Lisbon for two days.

items.explain: You can't buy them at the castle on Sundays.
